title: A cache in front of the database, and the invalidation it inherits

videos.script: A dashboard that takes four milliseconds is fast. Asked five thousand times a minute, it is most of what the database does. {{dashboard}} A cache keeps the answer somewhere quicker, so the next person gets the stored copy instead of the work. In this lesson the somewhere is Redis, and the copy is a seller's dashboard. {{redis}} You measure it first: thirteen times faster, and the database asked one time in twenty-five. {{measure}} Then you pay for it. Every cached answer is a copy, and a copy can be out of date. You watch a new order stay invisible for a minute, exactly as the cache promised. {{ttl}} You delete the key when the data changes, and find the race that writes the old value straight back. {{race}} You let a popular key expire under fifty readers at once, and the database runs the same count fifty times. Then you let only one of them do it. {{stampede}} Last, a cache that lives inside PostgreSQL itself, refreshed while people keep reading. {{matview}} The question under all of it is the same. How old an answer can this screen afford to show? {{title}}
